items.title: How Oracle Uses Codex to Help Business Users Get Answers
items.content_snippet: Richard Lam, Group Vice President at Oracle Applications Lab, shares how his team uses Codex to help business users get answers from company data. By describing the outcome they want, users can get an analysis, a report, or an application, with Codex gathering the information from internal systems. Read the full Oracle story: https://openai.com/index/oracle/

items.title: Building Self-Learning Loops for Your Agent — Fuad Ali, Arize AI
items.content_snippet: A shopping assistant confidently returns products outside a user's budget because its price filter is broken. Fuad Ali uses the Wonder Toys assistant to show how a production failure can become a complete improvement loop: collect the trace, investigate the code, propose a fix and test it against the cases that failed. items.title: Can Your Agent Hear You Now? Building Live Voice Agents with Gemini — Thor Schaeff
items.content_snippet: An agent that hears you, sees you, and answers in your language, in real time. Here's how to build one with Gemini. Thor Schaeff, who works on developer experience at Google DeepMind, runs a set of live demos of Gemini's real-time and media models. He builds an illustrated story with Gemini Live and a fast Nano Banana image model, using the stateful Interactions API to keep characters and style consistent between images. items.title: Agent Speedrun — Elizabeth Fuentes Leone & Sandhya Subramani, AWS
items.content_snippet: A customer service agent looks up an account, checks an order, and handles a refund. The harder part is controlling what happens between those steps and keeping that control when the agent reaches production. Elizabeth Fuentes Leone and Sandhya Subramani build the workflow with Strands Agents, starting with a system prompt and three tools backed by mock customer data. items.title: The SDLC You Build Yourself — Andy Wong, Andrei Bocan & Shane Wolf, Atlassian
items.content_snippet: An engineering standard becomes a reusable code review rule, applied across selected repositories instead of enforced by hand on every pull request. Andy Wong demonstrates that workflow with a design token standard while Andrei Bocan and Shane Wolf explain the context and orchestration underneath it. items.title: Agents That Own Their Inference — Du'an Lightfoot & Khaja Omer, Akamai Technologies
items.content_snippet: Speculative decoding drops a demo model from roughly 58 tokens per second to 16 instead of speeding it up. Du'an Lightfoot and Khaja Omer use that failed optimization to make a practical point: a faster inference configuration has to be measured against the actual model, hardware and workload. Their workshop starts with the decision to use hosted APIs or run inference on dedicated GPUs, then gives participants a Kubernetes namespace containing a Jupyter notebook and a vLLM endpoint. items.title: AI Security Engineer Foundations + Certificate — Micah Silverman, Snyk
items.content_snippet: A student chatbot refuses to reveal grades, but its refusal exposes that it has access to them. Micah Silverman uses that capture the flag exercise to connect AI risks with familiar application security controls. A system prompt telling an assistant to keep data private leaves the data within reach; a restricted database view removes it from the model's available context. The six module course covers OWASP risks, shadow AI, threat modeling, MCP security, secure agentic development and red teamin

items.title: Vector Isn't Enough: Hybrid Search & Retrieval — Jeff Vestal & James Williams, Elastic
items.content_snippet: An agent diagnoses exit code 137 by retrieving documentation, explaining an out of memory failure, and pointing to settings that can prevent it. Its answer depends on the search results it receives, and its citations lead back to the underlying documents. Jeff Vestal and James Williams work backward from that agent behavior to the retrieval layer in Elasticsearch. items.title: The Data Context Layer for Agents — Yoni Michael & Brandon Callender, Typedef
items.content_snippet: Two Rust types are both called PostingList, but changing them breaks different code. A text search finds both; a context graph preserves their identities and exposes their separate dependencies. Yoni Michael and Brandon Callender use that distinction to connect data engineering and coding agents. For a data system, valid SQL can still produce the wrong answer when a join multiplies rows or a refactor changes a metric's meaning. items.title: Turning My Obsidian Vault Into a Local AI Engineer — Filip Makraduli, Superlinked
items.content_snippet: A scanned NDA becomes a redacted Markdown document before a coding agent uses its contents. Filip Makraduli builds that workflow around an Obsidian vault, an MCP integration and Superlinked's inference engine, with small open models doing document processing on infrastructure the team controls. The starting problem combines sensitive files, expensive context and the need to adapt models to a particular task. items.title: Parsing the Epstein Files for JMail — Palak Agarwal & Omar Alhait, Reducto
items.content_snippet: Handwritten flight logs and heavily redacted PDFs stand between a pile of documents and a searchable product. Palak Agarwal and Omar Alhait show how Reducto turned the Epstein files into structured data for JMail and its related applications. Agarwal introduces the document processing layer; Alhait walks through the extraction pipeline behind JFlights, showing how a schema turns difficult pages into usable records.
